name: Jackson Pr. 12.9: Van Allen equator
description: Jackson Problem 12.9 (the Van Allen belts). In the equatorial plane of a dipole Earth the field grows towards the Earth, and a gyrating particle drifts around it: protons one way, electrons the other (the gradient drift of §12.4). A proton and an electron start at the same place; the proton must reach the northern satellite, the electron the southern one. Shift their drift shells with charges or magnets.

reality.represents: Drift around a dipole Earth: the Van Allen belts (Jackson Pr. 12.9)

remarks.line: Protons and electrons drift opposite ways
remarks.detail: The field grows towards the Earth, so a gyrating particle's orbit is tighter on the near side and it drifts around the Earth, the two signs in opposite senses: the ring current.
Near the Earth its field is close to a dipole's, which a magnetized sphere at the centre gives exactly.
Here a gyration is 0.4 of the distance to the Earth; a real belt particle gyrates over kilometres thousands of kilometres out, and drifts round in minutes to hours.
The particles stay in the equatorial plane. Real trapped particles also spiral along the field lines and bounce between mirror points in the north and the south.
